# Ledger 1.3 is out

## Check your Bun version before you update

Ledger 1.3 needs Bun 1.2 or later.
To see which version you have, run `bun --version`.
If the version is older than 1.2, run `bun upgrade` before you update Ledger.

## Payments are no longer imported twice when the payee is written differently

Ledger skips a payment that is already in `ledger.csv`.
Ledger 1.2 missed the duplicate when the payee name had different capital letters or extra spaces at the start or end, such as "Coffee Shop" and " coffee shop ".
Ledger 1.3 treats these names as the same payee.

Two payments now count as the same when they have the same date, the same amount to the cent, and the same payee.
When Ledger compares payees, it ignores capital letters and spaces at the start or end of the name.

## Preview an import before it changes your books

To see what an import would add without changing anything, run the import with `--dry-run`:

```sh
bun run import --dry-run <file>
```

Replace `<file>` with the path to your bank export.
Ledger lists the transactions the import would add and writes nothing to `ledger.csv`.
When the list looks right, run the same command without `--dry-run`.

## Import Alfa-Bank exports without column mapping

Ledger 1.3 reads Alfa-Bank exports as the bank saves them.
You no longer need to map their columns in `ledger.config.json`.

## Import files up to 50 MB

Each file you import can now be up to 50 MB.
The limit in Ledger 1.2 was 10 MB.

## See which columns are missing

When a file lacks columns that Ledger needs, Ledger reports a `MISSING_COLUMNS` error.
In Ledger 1.3, that error lists the missing columns, so you know what to look for in the export.
